public_rationale: The January 2025 chess study reports an Elo rating of 1788 for a specially trained ChessLLM, evaluated against reduced-strength Stockfish settings [e1]. It does not establish how contemporary general-purpose LLMs compare with full-strength chess engines, and it cannot settle the three-domain claim [e1].
limitations: The packet supplies no qualifying protein-structure or database-execution comparison.
The chess evidence establishes neither parity nor inferiority for contemporary general-purpose LLMs against competent specialist engines.
Missing comparisons do not establish that the claim is false.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs can't play chess, fold proteins, or run databases as well as conventional or special-purpose systems.

statement.excerpt: (They also can’t play chess as well as conventional algorithms, can’t fold proteins like special-purpose neurosymbolic hybrids, can’t run databases as well as conventional databases, etc.)

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading compares general-purpose LLMs performing these tasks themselves with competent specialist systems. Calling a chess engine or database does not establish the LLM's own performance.
Assess chess playing strength, protein-structure prediction accuracy, and database-operation correctness and performance separately. Supporting the entire statement requires evidence for all three.

The present-tense statement describes capabilities available before the post. With no standard capability-reporting period, use calendar 2025 through June 7 as the contemporary observation window; older results are context.
The claim does not establish that the specialist protein systems are correctly classified as neurosymbolic.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evaluations of contemporary general-purpose LLMs show materially inferior performance to competent specialist systems in all three named domains.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evaluations establish that contemporary general-purpose LLMs match or exceed competent specialist systems in one or more named domains. Report which component is contradicted; do not infer the other components.

evidence.locator: Section 6, Conclusion; comparison settings in Sections 4 and 5
evidence.explanation: The paper reports a fine-tuned chess model competing against reduced-strength Stockfish settings. It establishes meaningful chess capability, but neither parity with full-strength engines nor the performance of contemporary general-purpose LLMs.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Reproducible comparisons applicable to January 1–June 7, 2025, specifying model versions, specialist baselines, resources, and tool access. Tests should measure full-game chess strength, experimentally grounded protein-structure accuracy, and database execution correctness and performance. Inferiority in all three domains would support the whole claim; parity or superiority in any domain would contradict that component.
